questions.q: How is 'Knitting' best defined in fabric crafts?
options: The method of creating a continuous fabric by interlocking a series of loops made from a single yarn.
The practice of pressing heated wax onto a cotton cloth.
The traditional interlacing of warp and weft threads on a heavy loom.
The tying of fabrics to resist chemical dyes.
questions.explain: Knitting constructs fabric by pulling continuous loops of a single yarn through previously created loops, usually utilizing specialized needles.

questions.q: Which primary tool is used to carry out traditional hand knitting?
options: Two long, pointed knitting needles or pins
questions.explain: Hand knitting traditionally requires a pair of long, smooth, pointed knitting needles (sometimes called knitting pins) to hold the active loops and pull the yarn through.

questions.q: The main consumable raw material used in knitting warm garments like sweaters is:
questions.explain: Soft, thick, continuous strings of fiber known as yarn or wool are the essential raw materials required for knitting textiles.
questions.exam: BECE Cultural & Creative Arts: Textile Crafts, Packaging & Art Marketing
questions.subject: Cultural and Creative Arts

questions.q: What is the key difference between weaving and knitting?
options: Weaving is done on paper, while knitting is done on metal.
Knitting uses a single interlocking yarn to create elastic loops, while weaving crosses two sets of threads (warp and weft) at right angles.
Knitting requires a large mechanical loom, while weaving only requires two hand pins.
Weaving uses yarn, but knitting uses solid plastics.
questions.explain: Weaving involves intersecting two distinct sets of threads over and under each other. Knitting involves manipulating a single thread into consecutive, flexible loops.

questions.q: In hand knitting, what are the names of the two foundational stitches that form the basis of most patterns?
questions.explain: The Knit stitch (which looks like a small 'V') and the Purl stitch (which creates a horizontal bump) are the two fundamental mechanics that constitute almost all knitted fabrics.
questions.exam: BECE Cultural & Creative Arts: Textile Crafts, Packaging & Art Marketing

questions.q: Which of the following clothing items is most traditionally produced using the knitting process?
questions.explain: Knitting provides thick, warm, and highly elastic fabrics, making it the perfect method for producing winter wear like sweaters, cardigans, socks, and beanies.

questions.q: A student drops an active stitch off the needle while knitting, causing a vertical line of loops to unravel downwards. This occurrence is often called a:
questions.explain: A dropped stitch happens when an unsecured loop slides off the needle, causing the interlocked column of stitches beneath it to unravel, which creates a ladder-like hole.
